statement: This state estimates career resilience for a worker who actively uses frontier AI, keeps skills current, and deliberately moves toward high-context/high-accountability work. It is not a forecast for a worker who ignores AI.

crossRoleFindings.finding: Current evidence supports transformation and task/headcount compression more strongly than near-term wholesale occupation disappearance.
Entry-level and routine digital work is an early pressure point; current labor data does not establish broad software-engineering displacement.
AI capability on well-specified technical tasks is advancing rapidly, but benchmark task horizons are not equivalent to autonomous performance in messy real jobs.

AI-native workers can remain highly valuable even in exposed roles if they own verification, context, architecture, security, production and decisions that organizations are unwilling or unable to delegate fully.

globalProtectionStrategy: Use AI at the frontier; do not compete with it on raw mechanical output.
Shift toward problem framing, architecture, verification, security, production reliability, domain context and accountable decisions.
Build real evidence that you can operate and recover systems, not only generate artifacts.
Maintain fundamentals deeply enough to detect when an AI answer is wrong.
Track junior/routine-task compression separately from total role demand.
Keep optionality across adjacent roles instead of betting on one title for 20 years.

sources.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — 2025–35 occupational projections
sources.note: Official U.S. structural employment projection; not a global forecast.

sources.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — AI exposure categories
sources.note: Relative theoretical/observed AI exposure. BLS explicitly says exposure is not employment growth, adoption, productivity or replacement probability.

sources.name: ILO/NASK — Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index
sources.note: Task-level global exposure research; transformation is judged more likely than wholesale replacement for most occupations.

sources.name: World Economic Forum — Future of Jobs Report 2025
sources.note: Directional employer expectations through 2030; AI/big data and networks/cybersecurity are among fastest-growing skill groups.

sources.name: METR — Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
sources.note: Measures frontier-agent reliability on well-specified software/ML/cyber tasks; not equivalent to autonomous real-world jobs.

sources.name: LinkedIn Economic Graph — AI Labor Market Update, August 2026
sources.note: Cross-market hiring analysis. Entry-level hiring in AI-augmented roles such as software engineering showed additional weakness versus the role total, while AI Engineer remained fast-growing.

sources.name: LinkedIn Economic Graph — U.S. Software Engineer Talent Landscape 2026
sources.note: Finds tightening SWE entry pathways and growing AI/cloud skill emphasis while evidence of broad AI displacement of SWE remains scarce.

sources.name: Anthropic Economic Index — Cadences
sources.note: Real Claude usage plus linked survey. Useful for adoption/worker-expectation evidence; provider-user population is not the labor market as a whole.

roles.name: AI-Native Product Engineer

facts: Software Developers: +10.2% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
AI-related roles and skills remain among the strongest growth signals, but there is no one-to-one official occupation for this composite role.

roles.aiTransformation: Implementation, research, prototyping and routine integration are rapidly cheaper. The defensible center shifts toward product judgment, architecture, evaluation, security, business context and end-to-end ownership.
loadBearingHumanWork: Problem framing and requirements under ambiguity
End-to-end ownership across agents and humans

Y1.summary: Near-term risk is mostly task compression, not AI-only role replacement.

Y5.summary: Agents can absorb more implementation; value concentrates in ownership and system judgment.

Y10.summary: High automation is plausible, but product/accountability boundaries remain meaningful.

Y20.summary: 20-year range is a stress test; conclusions depend on autonomy, liability and organization redesign.

riskUpSignposts: Agents reliably own multi-week product work with low supervision
Organizations measurably remove product-engineering layers rather than redeploying them
Evaluation/security/accountability become largely machine-owned
riskDownSignposts: High-value systems continue to require accountable human owners
Integration/reliability/security remain bottlenecks
AI increases number of viable products and demand for builders
protectionPlaybook: Become excellent at agent orchestration plus verification, not prompting alone
Own requirements, architecture, data, security and production trade-offs
Build evidence of operating systems after launch
Learn to measure AI quality/cost/latency/failure modes
Keep direct product/business communication ability

roles.name: Full-Stack / Product Engineer

facts: Software Developers: +10.2% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
Web Developers: +3.8% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
Entry pathways are tightening and AI/cloud capabilities are gaining weight.

roles.aiTransformation: Routine CRUD, UI implementation, tests and code translation are increasingly automatable; product context, architecture, integration and responsibility become more important.

Y1.summary: Strong augmentation already; AI-only replacement remains limited by context and ownership.

Y5.summary: Routine implementation compresses significantly; stronger builders cover more surface area.

Y10.summary: Generalist coding becomes much cheaper; durable value shifts toward product/system ownership.

Y20.summary: Long-run survival depends on whether accountable product ownership remains human.

riskUpSignposts: AI agents handle full-stack changes across mature repos with minimal review
Companies consistently reduce engineer counts per product without offsetting product expansion
riskDownSignposts: Product scope expands as building gets cheaper
Production/security/accountability continue to require experienced humans
protectionPlaybook: Move from ticket execution to product/system ownership
Strengthen architecture, databases, production and security
Use AI to increase scope per person while keeping verification skill
Maintain strong user/client communication

roles.name: Software Engineer

facts: Software Developers: +10.2% projected U.S. employment 2025–35 with ~95.3k annual openings in the PAS labor baseline.
LinkedIn 2026 data shows weaker entry pathways but scarce evidence of broad SWE displacement so far.

roles.aiTransformation: Code generation is becoming a commodity faster than engineering judgment. Junior/routine work is the first pressure point; complex systems, verification and ownership are more resilient.

Y1.summary: The current pressure is strongest on routine and entry-level work.

Y5.summary: Fewer engineers may produce the same software; stronger AI-native engineers remain valuable.

Y10.summary: AI-only engineering becomes plausible for more bounded systems; high-context work remains harder.

Y20.summary: The 20-year outcome hinges on general agent autonomy and organizational willingness to remove human accountability.

riskUpSignposts: Long-horizon agents reliably change large real repos without human decomposition
Senior review/architecture becomes machine-dominant
SWE hiring decouples downward from overall tech demand for several years
riskDownSignposts: Software demand expands faster than productivity reduces headcount
Human verification remains necessary for consequential systems
protectionPlaybook: Do not compete on raw code output
Deepen architecture, debugging, testing, data and production
Be able to verify AI output independently
Build domain context and ownership evidence
Use AI to work across a wider system, not only faster inside one ticket

roles.name: Systems Analyst / Software Architect

facts: Computer Systems Analysts: +7.9% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
Database Architects: +9.4% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.

roles.aiTransformation: AI accelerates modeling, documentation and option generation, but ambiguous requirements, cross-system trade-offs, governance and accountability remain load-bearing.

Y1.summary: Architecture is augmented heavily but still context/accountability bound.

Y5.summary: AI can propose designs; trusted ownership and cross-organizational context remain defensible.

Y10.summary: More architecture synthesis may automate, but responsibility and tacit constraints matter.

Y20.summary: A very autonomous future could compress architects, but governance/liability may preserve humans.

riskUpSignposts: AI reliably elicits requirements and negotiates constraints with stakeholders
Organizations delegate architecture liability and change approval to AI
riskDownSignposts: Regulation/accountability keeps named human owners
Legacy integration and organizational constraints remain dominant
protectionPlaybook: Develop requirements/decision quality, not diagram production
Own migrations, trade-offs and failure modes
Build security/privacy/governance depth
Practice explaining and defending decisions to nontechnical stakeholders

roles.name: Applied AI Engineer

facts: WEF places AI/ML specialists and AI/big-data skills among the strongest growth signals through 2030.
LinkedIn 2026 reports AI Engineer among fast-growing occupations in multiple markets.
There is no clean one-to-one BLS occupation for Applied AI Engineer.

roles.aiTransformation: Demand is strong because firms are adopting AI, but the tools used by AI engineers are themselves increasingly agentic. Durable value shifts to evaluation, integration, data, reliability, cost, security and domain outcomes.

Y1.summary: Current demand is strong; self-automation mostly increases leverage.

Y5.summary: Commodity AI integration compresses; deeper runtime/eval work remains defensible.

Y10.summary: If agents build and operate AI systems themselves, general integration roles narrow.

Y20.summary: Long-run risk is high precisely because this role works closest to the automation frontier.

riskUpSignposts: Model providers absorb most retrieval/evals/agent infrastructure into managed products
Agents autonomously run experiments, deploy and monitor AI systems with low supervision
riskDownSignposts: Model heterogeneity, regulation, security and domain integration keep system engineering complex
AI deployment expands into many more organizations and use cases
protectionPlaybook: Go beyond API integration into evals, observability, grounding and safety
Own production economics: latency, cost, reliability
Build domain-specific AI systems with measurable outcomes
Maintain strong software/data/security foundations

roles.name: Data Engineer

facts: Database Architects: +9.4% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
WEF identifies big data among the strongest growth areas.

roles.aiTransformation: SQL generation, pipeline scaffolding and routine transformations automate quickly; data contracts, lineage, quality, governance, distributed reliability and business semantics remain harder.

Y1.summary: Routine pipeline work is increasingly automated but production data ownership remains important.

Y5.summary: Smaller teams can operate more pipelines; robust platform/data ownership differentiates.

Y10.summary: AI may automate substantial implementation while governance and semantics persist.

Y20.summary: Autonomous data platforms could compress heavily; consequential data ownership may remain human.

riskUpSignposts: Autonomous data platforms handle schema evolution, incidents and governance reliably
Organizations standardize data layers enough to remove integration complexity
riskDownSignposts: Data quality, access, lineage and domain semantics remain chronic bottlenecks
Regulation increases accountable data ownership
protectionPlaybook: Master modeling, transactions, quality and governance
Own platform reliability/cost/security
Learn semantic/domain modeling, not only pipeline syntax
Use AI for SQL/scaffolding but verify data correctness

roles.name: Data Scientist

facts: Data Scientists: +34.6% projected U.S. employment 2025–35 with ~24.8k annual openings in the PAS labor baseline.
WEF identifies big-data roles/skills among strong growth areas.

roles.aiTransformation: Exploratory coding, model selection, feature ideation and reporting automate rapidly. Problem formulation, causal/statistical judgment, experiment design, data validity and business decisions remain more defensible.

Y1.summary: Demand is strong, but routine analysis/modeling is already highly AI-augmentable.

Y5.summary: General modeling work compresses; rigorous decision science and domain depth matter more.

Y10.summary: Automated research/modeling can absorb much of routine data science.

Y20.summary: Long-run role survives mainly if human decision ownership/causal judgment stays valuable.

riskUpSignposts: AI autonomously performs trustworthy end-to-end analysis with robust causal/statistical validation
AutoML/agents make bespoke modeling commodity across firms
riskDownSignposts: Real-world experimentation, causality, regulation and domain stakes retain human accountability
Demand for data-driven decisions expands faster than automation
protectionPlaybook: Prioritize statistics, causality and experiment design over notebook mechanics
Own data quality and business decision framing
Build production/evaluation literacy
Communicate uncertainty and consequences clearly

roles.name: Data Analyst / BI

facts: This profile has no direct BLS row in the current PAS baseline.
Digitized analytical/clerical task families are among those most exposed to GenAI transformation; routine querying/reporting is especially automatable.

roles.aiTransformation: Natural-language querying, dashboard generation, recurring reports and descriptive analysis are directly exposed. Resilience comes from domain semantics, metric governance, decision support and ownership of ambiguous business questions.

Y1.summary: Routine reporting and querying are already highly exposed.

Y5.summary: Large compression is plausible for dashboard/report-centric roles.

Y10.summary: A smaller number of domain-heavy analysts may cover much more work.

Y20.summary: Pure reporting/BI execution is a high-risk long-run shape; domain decision roles are more resilient.

riskUpSignposts: Semantic layers plus agents reliably answer business questions without analyst mediation
Self-service AI analytics becomes trusted for consequential decisions
riskDownSignposts: Organizations continue to struggle with metric definitions/data quality
Analysts own domain decisions, experimentation or operational change rather than reports
protectionPlaybook: Move away from dashboard production as the core identity
Own metrics, semantics and business decisions
Deepen SQL/data modeling enough to audit AI answers
Add experimentation/causal reasoning or data engineering adjacency

roles.name: Platform / Production Engineer (DevOps/SRE)

facts: Computer Network Architects: +7.7% projected U.S. employment 2025–35.
Networks/cybersecurity remain among WEF fastest-growing skill groups.

roles.aiTransformation: Runbooks, config, diagnostics and remediation can automate deeply. Resilience comes from reliability ownership, failure judgment, security, cost, distributed-systems reasoning and incident accountability.

Y1.summary: Automation reduces toil; accountability for production remains strongly human.

Y5.summary: Autonomous remediation can reduce headcount, but high-stakes ownership persists.

Y10.summary: Many operational loops may become autonomous; system design/failure ownership differentiates.

Y20.summary: Long-term resilience depends on whether organizations allow AI to own consequential production decisions.

riskUpSignposts: Autonomous operations proves reliable through major incidents
Cloud platforms absorb most SRE/platform engineering decisions
riskDownSignposts: Complex distributed failures and security remain hard
Regulation/business risk requires accountable human operators
protectionPlaybook: Own observability, incident response, backup/restore and failure drills
Deepen distributed systems and security
Automate toil aggressively while retaining diagnostic skill
Learn cost/capacity architecture

roles.name: Security Engineer / AppSec

facts: Information Security Analysts: +21% projected U.S. employment 2025–35 with ~14.1k annual openings in the PAS labor baseline.
Networks and cybersecurity are among WEF fastest-growing skill groups.

roles.aiTransformation: Scanning, triage, rule generation, code review and parts of offensive/defensive work automate. The attack surface also grows. Threat modeling, adversarial judgment, incident ownership, architecture and risk accountability remain stronger.

Y1.summary: Automation increases leverage while demand/security surface remains strong.

Y5.summary: Routine SOC/AppSec tasks compress, but adversarial/security ownership is durable.

Y10.summary: AI may automate much detection/response; accountable architecture and adversarial adaptation remain.

Y20.summary: Long-run risk is substantial but security is also recursively generated by more automation.

riskUpSignposts: Autonomous defenders outperform human teams across live adversarial environments
Liability/regulation permits AI-owned risk acceptance
riskDownSignposts: Attackers and defenders co-evolve, preserving adversarial human oversight
Security regulation increases named accountability
protectionPlaybook: Move from tool operation to threat modeling/AppSec/security architecture
Build incident and production experience
Understand identity, least privilege and trust boundaries deeply
Use AI for scanning/triage but independently validate security conclusions

roles.name: Technical Founder / Product Builder

facts: No single occupational projection represents founder/product-builder work.
Cheaper software/AI production may reduce build cost while increasing competition and the number of viable products.

roles.aiTransformation: Execution becomes cheaper, so differentiation shifts toward problem selection, customer insight, distribution, capital allocation, trust and strategic ownership. AI may eliminate many implementation constraints without eliminating entrepreneurship.
loadBearingHumanWork: Combining market, product and technical context

Y1.summary: AI mainly increases founder leverage in the near term.

Y5.summary: Building gets cheaper; competition rises, but ownership/market selection stays human-heavy.

Y10.summary: AI may run more companies operationally; human trust, risk and capital decisions still matter.

Y20.summary: A highly autonomous economy could change firm formation itself; this is a strategic stress test.

riskUpSignposts: AI agents autonomously discover markets, sell, negotiate and allocate capital better than human founders
Trust/ownership/legal systems accept machine-run firms broadly
riskDownSignposts: Human relationships, ownership and legal accountability remain central
Cheaper building expands entrepreneurship and niche markets
protectionPlaybook: Develop customer/distribution skill alongside technical leverage
Use AI to multiply execution, not outsource problem selection
Build decision quality and capital allocation discipline
Own trust, brand, relationships and strategy

limitations: The scenario percentage ranges are not calibrated probabilities of unemployment or role extinction.
The 10-year and especially 20-year bands are intentionally broad and should be treated as stress tests.
U.S. BLS projections are structural benchmarks, not Argentina or global forecasts.
LinkedIn and Anthropic datasets have platform/population selection effects.
Provider usage evidence is useful for adoption patterns but is not independent proof of provider capability claims.
Personal resilience depends on actual skill/evidence development, not merely identifying as AI-native.
